patch.objective: Use the CIWA-Ar scale for alcohol withdrawal and recognize alcohol overdose

sources.note: Relayed from the ADN-RN course's earlier cases (read 2026-11-11, primary PDF), not re-read for this band: the pre-licensure RN course is built toward this test plan.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case alcohol-withdrawal-ciwa, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the REQ-233 NCLEX-RN cases (read 2026-11-11, primary PDF), not re-read: Psychosocial Integrity includes chemical and other dependencies (withdrawal and toxicity); Reduction of Risk Potential includes recognizing changes in the client's condition.

sources.cite: American Society of Addiction Medicine. The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management (adopted 2020-01-23)
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case alcohol-withdrawal-ciwa, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-16 in the primary PDF through a summarizing fetch with quotes (the first part of the document): mild withdrawal 'e.g., CIWA-Ar score <10', moderate 'CIWA-Ar scores 10-18', severe at 19 (the comparison sign was lost in the extracted text); symptom-triggered treatment is the preferred benzodiazepine dosing method (V.23); reassess every 1-4 hours for 24 hours as clinically indicated (V.1); thiamine 100 mg IV or IM daily for 3-5 days is typical, and thiamine and glucose may be given in any order (V.7); a history of withdrawal delirium or withdrawal seizure raises the risk of complicated withdrawal (II.5), and when that risk is known treat more aggressively (VII.13); restraints only when required to prevent injury from agitation or violence (VI.12).

sources.cite: StatPearls. Alcohol withdrawal (point-of-care chapter 17335), StatPearls Publishing
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case alcohol-withdrawal-ciwa, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch with quotes; the page did not show its title or update date: signs may begin within hours of the last drink and peak around 72 hours; withdrawal seizures 'typically occur between 8 and 48 hours'; delirium tremens 3 to 8 days after cessation (the page also says 3 to 5).

sources.cite: Southern Health-Sante Sud. Alcohol Withdrawal Assessment Flowsheet (CIWA-Ar), form CLI.5110.SG.013.FORM.02 (2024-01-19)
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case alcohol-withdrawal-ciwa, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch: ten items (nausea and vomiting, tremor, anxiety, agitation, paroxysmal sweats, tactile, auditory and visual disturbances, headache, each 0-7; orientation 0-4; 67 at most); PRN medication for a total of 10 or higher under the symptom-triggered method. Used for the items and the trigger; one hospital's form, not a guideline.
